AMZN.rationale: Amazon's franchise quality is elite — AWS at 18% of revenue but ~57% of operating income, advertising at $68.5B growing ~22%, and a dominant ~40.5% US e-commerce share create a durable, self-reinforcing flywheel. Q1 2026 was a standout quarter: revenue $181.5B (+17% YoY), operating margin a record 13.1%, and AWS reaccelerated to 28% growth. The balance sheet is strong (D/E 0.149, equity $369.6B) and operating cash flow is exceptional at $35.5B/quarter and growing. However, two material concerns cap the score. First, operating income declined QoQ in Q3 2025 ($19.17B→$17.42B, -9.1%) while revenue grew +7.4%, and net income exceeded operating income by $3.77B due to non-operating items — a pattern recurring into Q1 2026 (Rivian gains). Second, at 34.2x trailing PE with a 2.9% earnings yield 155bp below the 10-year Treasury, the stock demands continued earnings acceleration that the operating-margin trend does not cleanly support. FCF collapsed 95% to $1.2B TTM as $200B+ capex is deployed into AI infrastructure, and long-term debt nearly doubled to $127.3B. Two high-profile investors (Berkshire, Druckenmiller) exited on valuation. The franchise is strong enough to warrant a modest positive score, but the earnings-quality issue, rate headwind, and massive capex cycle create enough uncertainty to keep the score moderate rather than strong. The Q2 2026 earnings report (guided $194B-$199B revenue) is a credible near-term catalyst that could re-rate the stock if operating leverage improves.

PE 34.2x (range 28.2-39.0 over 365d) with earnings yield 2.9% vs 10-year Treasury 4.45% — negative equity risk premium of -155bp
Berkshire Hathaway fully exited and Druckenmiller sold 94% of Amazon stake in Q1 2026, citing valuation

FTC monopolization trial set for October 2026; EU DMA gatekeeper designation; rising regulatory headwinds
